acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The car estimate requires a familiar mass and speed plus one kinetic-energy calculation.

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Students must identify the surviving velocity component and square it in the kinetic-energy ratio.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Scaling kinetic energy linearly with speed

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Students must use force balance at both speeds and scale the drag between them.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Adding gravity and drag as if they act in the same direction

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Students must determine the acceleration direction and eliminate the spring constant using the initial compression.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Treating upward motion as upward acceleration

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Students must identify the angle between velocity vectors and use their vector difference to calculate impulse.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Ignoring the horizontal change in momentum

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Students must apply Newton’s laws to the whole system and to one block in isolation.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Confusing the net force on a block with the contact force

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Students must determine the lever arms and opposing moments of both tension components and the beam’s weight.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Using the full beam length for the weight’s lever arm

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Students must infer the mass’s speed from the fraction of potential energy converted to kinetic energy.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Assuming kinetic energy is proportional to speed

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Students must translate the steady decrease in radius into the shape of a speed–time graph.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Equating constant angular velocity with constant linear speed

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Students must identify the shared geostationary orbit and distinguish its radius from its altitude.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Confusing orbital radius with height above Earth

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Students must relate the two orbital radii through their common gravitational force, then calculate both kinetic energies.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using a star’s orbital radius as the separation in the gravitational force

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Students must distinguish temperature, internal energy and net energy transfer at equilibrium.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Confusing zero net energy transfer with no exchange

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Students must include atmospheric pressure at both depths and use the inverse pressure–volume relation.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Ignoring atmospheric pressure at the bottom

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The speeds can be substituted directly into the definition of root mean square speed.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Taking the average outside the square root

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Students must identify the zero-normal-force threshold and link it to the largest downward SHM acceleration.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Missing the zero-normal-force condition at the contact limit

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The graph follows directly from the restoring-force relation.

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must undo the vertical projection and square the recovered amplitude.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Taking the angle from the wrong axis

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must infer the wavelength from the spacing of successive resonances.

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must connect the added phase delay to the direction of the fringe shift.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Confusing fringe shift with fringe spacing

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must check field directions and compare inverse-square magnitudes.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Ignoring the directions of the fields

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The diagram requires interpreting the initial deflection and comparing equipotential spacings.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Assuming a delay before the electric force acts

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must combine the resistance and density equations before comparing masses.

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The options require reading the same graph under fixed-current, series and parallel conditions.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Using tangent slope to find resistance

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must obtain the solenoid field from the vector triangle before calculating the current.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Confusing total turns with turns per metre

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish circulation around the full frame from circulation in the two subloops.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Treating the flux change in one subloop as a change through the whole frame

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Each setting follows from dividing a known quantity by its span on the trace.

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The false statement follows directly from the inverse energy–wavelength relation.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Associating shorter wavelengths with lower photon energies

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish the intrinsic trade-off from experimental limits and read the bound precisely.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Treating quantum uncertainty as an equipment limitation

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must account for all neutron masses, convert units and apply mass–energy equivalence.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Omitting free neutrons from the mass balance

acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must obtain the decay constant from the logarithmic plot before calculating the half-life.
acjc-2022-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Halving the logarithm instead of the count rate

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Students must break several familiar derived units into base units.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Counting powers instead of distinct base units.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Students must translate the force profile into the changing slope of a speed graph.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Students need to compare a triangle and a trapezium on a speed–time graph.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Using the speed at one instant in place of the area.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Students must calculate the velocity change and then find the range of possible vector sums.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Treating change in velocity as a scalar.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Students must resolve the weight and assign signs to both forces along the slope.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Assigning friction the same direction as the downhill motion.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Students must identify both moment arms and track the sense of each moment.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Losing the sign of a moment.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Students must resolve three forces, find their resultant and reverse its direction.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Reporting the resultant instead of the balancing force.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Students must link constant power to a falling pulling force and then to the gradient of the speed graph.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Equating constant power with constant force.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Students must distinguish shared angular speed from radius-dependent speed and centripetal force.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Confusing linear speed and angular speed.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Students must connect the equal mutual forces to the two orbital radii before calculating the force.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using the separation as either star’s orbital radius.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Students must establish or recall the period–radius scaling and apply it relative to Earth.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Confusing the scaling of orbital period with its square.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Students must connect constant temperature with mean kinetic energy and account for energy absorbed on melting.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Equating constant temperature with constant internal energy.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Students must combine escape energy with the mean kinetic energy per helium atom and convert the diameter to metres.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Treating the planetary diameter as the radius.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Students must choose the post-leak state and use the absolute hot temperature.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Treating the temperature increase as the final temperature.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The presence of repeated cycles with decreasing amplitude identifies the damping regime.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Inferring the damping regime from the liquid’s viscosity alone.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: It tests the basic distinction between the driving and natural frequencies.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Confusing driving frequency with natural frequency

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must turn a travel-time difference into a fraction of a cycle.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Using half a cycle as the radian conversion factor

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The grating equation gives the order limit, which must be converted into a count on both sides.

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must recognize what the change in air-column length measures.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Confusing resonance spacing with a full wavelength

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: It combines scalar potential cancellation with the work–energy relation.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Confusing electric potential with electric field

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must use the full plate separation and then apply the electron charge.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Using potential in place of electric field

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must trace the conducting paths for several switch settings.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Overlooking a bypass around a resistor

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: It links the paper width to the slope of a cumulative voltage reading.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Confusing potential drop with local potential

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must identify the two forces forming the couple and their separation.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Confusing zero net force with zero torque

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Two distinct changes to the average power must be combined.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Treating power as proportional to current

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The calculation requires the angle to the coil normal and a square-unit conversion.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Using the coil plane in the cosine formula

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish how intensity and frequency affect different features of the graph.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Confusing photon energy with photon arrival rate

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: It requires linking electron momentum to kinetic energy and then photon wavelength.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Applying the electron de Broglie relation to the emitted X-ray

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: It asks for the standard inference from most alpha particles passing through the foil.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Confusing known projectile properties with experimental deductions

acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must convert binding energy per nucleon to total binding energy and take the difference.
acjc-2023-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Comparing binding energies per nucleon without tracking the nuclei

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Matching the time exponents requires expressing power and speed in base units.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must compare changes in gradient over the marked intervals.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The calculation requires comparing two displacements from release and resolving gravity along the incline.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Treating the block as stationary at the first sensor.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must turn a volume flow rate into a mass flow rate and then into a momentum rate.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Confusing mass flow rate with momentum flow rate.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Momentum conservation must be applied separately to the throw and catch with consistent signs.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Assuming Charlie and the returning ball move in opposite directions.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must resolve the tension using an angle measured from the vertical.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Swapping the sine and cosine components.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: A single moments equation determines the required ratio of the loads.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Assigning the larger load to the longer arm.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The calculation links density, gravitational energy, elapsed time and efficiency.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Multiplying useful output by efficiency to find input.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The only calculation is dividing one revolution in radians by the 12-hour period in seconds.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must apply both changes and account for the square of angular speed in the acceleration.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Assuming unchanged linear speed means unchanged centripetal acceleration.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must consider both the strength and direction of all three fields.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Rearranging the gas law exposes how the two changes combine in the graph gradient.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Treating gradient as proportional to the amount of gas and temperature.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must add two sensible heating terms and a latent heat term with consistent units.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Omitting the heating of the ice to its melting point.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The question asks for direct recall of the ideal-gas particle volume assumption.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Treating molecular volume as comparable to container volume.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish a fast nonoscillatory return from slower decay and oscillatory responses.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Equating any nonoscillatory decay with critical damping.

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Squaring the SHM speed relation gives the energy ratio directly.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Using the speed ratio as the energy ratio

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student counts compression intervals and substitutes into the wave equation.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Treating a compression-to-rarefaction interval as a wavelength

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student calculates the wavelength and recognises when a whole-cycle phase difference is equivalent.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Treating equivalent whole-cycle phases as distinct

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The Rayleigh criterion gives an immediate inverse-proportion calculation.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Assuming angular resolution increases with slit width

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student recognises scalar cancellation and calculates the remaining point-charge contribution.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Ignoring the sign of a charge when adding potentials

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student distinguishes the direction of falling potential from the change in field strength.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Confusing decreasing potential with decreasing field strength

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The central wires must be recognised as one node before the network can be reduced.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Counting resistors without identifying common nodes

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must convert the voltage drops on the two equal-length wires into graph slopes.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Assuming equal-length wires have equal voltage drops

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student compares the initial electric and magnetic force directions with the observed deflection.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming a magnetic force acts along the field

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must combine motional e.m.f., current and magnetic force, resolving components for both induction and force balance.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Applying the inclination factor only once

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must square and average a non-sinusoidal waveform before taking the square root.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Using the sinusoidal RMS factor for any alternating voltage

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish the effect of the work function on the threshold from the universal slope.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Assuming the work function changes the graph gradient

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish the voltage-dependent cutoff from a characteristic emission line.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Assuming tube voltage sets the characteristic wavelengths

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student applies the unchanged nuclear charge of an isotope to Rutherford scattering.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Assuming extra neutrons increase nuclear charge

acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student uses the relation between binding energy per nucleon and stability to compare the nuclei.
acjc-2024-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Assuming the heavier parent is more tightly bound per nucleon

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Subtracting two equal-length velocity vectors requires reading their directions from the path.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Treating final velocity as the change in velocity.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must compare the direction of drag and the resulting acceleration on each leg.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Assuming gravity makes the descent faster despite air resistance.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The calculation is direct once the two trailing carts are treated as one system.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Choosing the wrong carts for the system.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must check both momentum and relative speed against the pictured velocities.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Assuming momentum conservation alone guarantees elasticity.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must track the frictional loss and compare the initial and final heights.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Counting the dip depth as a net height change.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must identify the upward resultant and include the downward weight.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Equating the normal force with the centripetal resultant.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must find the diagonal distance and combine a vector field and a scalar potential differently.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Treating fields and potentials as if they add in the same way.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must relate orbital kinetic energy to potential energy before scaling with radius.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Using inverse-square scaling for gravitational potential energy.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must account for the gas initially present in both halves when the volume available to each portion doubles.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Treating one compartment as a vacuum.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish the inverse-mass scaling of mean-square speed from the scaling of RMS speed.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Treating RMS speed as inversely proportional to molecular mass.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must carry the same internal energy change across both paths and use the correct work signs.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Treating heat or work as fixed by the endpoints.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The question asks for the characteristic response of a heavily damped oscillator.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Confusing heavy damping with critical damping.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must read matching acceleration and displacement magnitudes and take a square root.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Reading the magnitude of the gradient as angular frequency.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must identify opposite phases from particle spacing in a longitudinal wave.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Confusing successive compressions with opposite phases.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must read a full cycle, apply the time-base scale and convert the frequency into a wavelength.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Treating the horizontal trace as distance travelled by the sound.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The main challenge is reading the truncated wavelength axis.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The calculation links angular resolution to linear separation using the small-angle approximation.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Students must locate the first node from an antinode before counting the remaining nodes.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Counting nodes from the wrong starting phase

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The graph follows directly from the uniform field and the fixed particle charge.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Assuming the force varies with distance between parallel plates

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Students compare familiar definitions and recognise that a field line crosses equipotentials.

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Students apply the current equation and square the diameter ratio to obtain the area ratio.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Using diameter instead of cross-sectional area

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The straight segment tempts students to confuse its inverse slope with the resistance at a point.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Reading resistance from the inverse tangent slope

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Students must recognise the two parallel groups and track how the voltage divides after a branch opens.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Treating a blown parallel lamp as an open circuit for both lamps

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Students apply the grip rule to several wires and combine the field directions by symmetry.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming equal currents produce the same resultant field at every midpoint

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Students must balance the force magnitudes and reverse the direction of the electric force to find the field.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Confusing the electric force direction with the field direction for an electron

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Students must recognise the rotating spoke as sweeping out flux at a constant rate and relate the rotation period to angular speed.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Using rim speed as the speed of the entire spoke

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Students must account for diode conduction over half the cycle before finding the RMS voltage and power.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Squaring the mean voltage instead of taking the mean square

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The calculation requires converting the photon energy to electronvolts and matching it to a level gap.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Matching photon energy to an energy level instead of a level difference

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Students distinguish the voltage-dependent spectral cutoff from the fixed wavelengths of the target's emission lines.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Assuming the accelerating voltage shifts characteristic lines

acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The intended answer relies on recognising the short range of alpha radiation in air.
acjc-2025-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Treating electric deflection as unique to alpha particles

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Needs the order of magnitude of a nuclear diameter and the speed of light, then one division.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Confusing the size of the nucleus with the size of the atom

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Qualitative application of centre of gravity and the zero-torque condition.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Thinking balance requires equal mass on each side or a support at the geometric centre

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires resolving tensions vertically and reasoning about the small-angle limit.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Assuming each string simply carries half the weight

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Single energy-conservation equation linking GPE to elastic PE.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Forgetting to square-root or forgetting the factor of 1/2 in elastic PE

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Standard idea that projectile motion without air resistance is independent of mass.

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Requires seeing that the seat supplies both the vertical support and the horizontal accelerating force, then combining vectors.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Taking only the horizontal or only the vertical component of the contact force

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Choose the right form of the acceleration formula when the period is fixed.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Using $a = v^2/r$ while treating $v$ as constant

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Must express mass in terms of density and radius before applying g = GM/r².
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Ignoring that the larger star also has more mass

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Needs total orbital energy (KE + GPE) at both radii and careful handling of signs and small differences.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Thinking that a slower satellite has lost energy, or using only KE or only GPE

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Direct substitution into the SHM energy formula with unit conversions.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using frequency f instead of angular frequency ω

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Must link resonance to the natural frequency and then combine with a given wave-speed formula.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Not recognising that maximum amplitude means driving frequency equals natural frequency

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Two simultaneous changes (amplitude via intensity ∝ A², and period) must be read off grids.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Thinking amplitude is proportional to intensity rather than its square root

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Forgetting that the first polariser halves unpolarised light, or using cos instead of cos²

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Small-angle single-slit relation with two simultaneous factor changes.

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires recognising that sin θ, not θ, scales with order, and recalling that higher orders are dimmer.

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Rayleigh criterion plus small-angle geometry with unit conversions.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Unit/power-of-ten errors with km and nm

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Recall of kinetic theory assumptions with one invalid statement to spot.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Confusing elastic collisions (no KE change) with no momentum change

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Direct ideal-gas ratio calculation with a Celsius-to-kelvin conversion.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Using Celsius temperatures instead of kelvin

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires reading start and end equipotentials of each path and knowing work is path-independent.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Thinking work done depends on the length of the path taken

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Recall that field strength is the negative potential gradient, read at a point on a graph.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Using V/x instead of the gradient, or dropping the minus sign

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Two-stage charge calculation: constant current plus a linearly falling current (area of a triangle).
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Forgetting to convert hours to seconds or treating the falling stage as full current

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires reading $R = V/I$ from the shape of four I–V curves.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Confusing resistance with the gradient of the I–V graph, or reversing the effect of a curve bending

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Recognise three resistors in parallel in series with one, then apply potential divider ratio.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Thinking the voltmeter reads the e.m.f. or splitting the e.m.f. equally between the four resistors

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Direct use of $F = BIl\sin\theta$ plus Fleming's left-hand rule.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Using $\cos\theta$ instead of $\sin\theta$, or misapplying Fleming's left-hand rule

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: One substitution into $F = Bqv$ plus recognising that a magnetic force does no work but changes momentum direction.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Thinking constant speed means momentum is unchanged

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Direct use of Faraday's law with flux linkage $NBA$.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Forgetting the number of turns or using diameter/final B only

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Find secondary current, then use the turns ratio for an ideal transformer.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Inverting the current ratio of a transformer (current steps the opposite way to voltage)

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Must link spatial extent of the wavefunction to $\Delta x$ and then use the uncertainty principle.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Thinking a localised wave packet has a well-defined momentum

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Pattern matching of line spectra; must check that all lines of an element appear.
acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Concluding an element is present when only some of its lines match

acjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Recognise that equal time intervals multiply activity by the same factor.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The joule is the only derived unit that needs to be expanded.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Using the dimensions of force for energy.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must handle both the exact coefficient and the squared denominator.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish a velocity–distance graph from a velocity–time graph.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Treating uniform deceleration as a constant slope on any velocity graph.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must compare initial slopes on the same scales and account for increasing drag.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Confusing initial velocity with the initial slope of a velocity–time graph.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must resolve both momentum vectors and track which signed component reverses.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Treating momentum change as the change in momentum magnitude.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must identify the shelf pivot and the perpendicular distance to the centre of gravity.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Using the vertical dimension as the lever arm of a vertical force.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must use the resultant force to find the kinetic energy gain per second.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Confusing engine output power with net mechanical power.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must convert the orbital data to SI units and use angular speed in the acceleration formula.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Omitting a factor of $2\pi$ when converting period to angular speed.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: One direct proportionality determines the shape and intercept of the graph.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Confusing a common angular speed with a common linear speed.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must use the inverse square-root relationship and measure radius from Earth's centre.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using altitude as the distance from Earth's centre.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish angular velocity from linear speed and recall the equatorial orbit requirement.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Equating linear speeds for two objects with the same angular velocity.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must infer equal pressures and account for simultaneous changes in volume and temperature.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Assuming that equal pressure also requires equal temperature.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must infer which sample warms more at equal mass and energy input.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Assuming equal heat inputs produce equal temperature rises.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must read the scaled axes, find the signed cycle area, and distinguish work on the gas from work by it.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Confusing work done on the gas with work done by it.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must connect the decay of amplitude with the shape of the total-energy curve.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Confusing changes in kinetic and potential energy with changes in total energy.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must infer instantaneous motion from a spatial snapshot.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Treating a zero crossing as a fixed node

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must combine unequal amplitudes before squaring their ratio.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Assuming all destructive interference gives zero intensity

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must calculate the observed angle and compare it with the diffraction limit.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Confusing angular separation with the resolution limit

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must infer the field direction from equilibrium and track both potential energies.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Confusing reduced plate voltage with reduced particle potential energy

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must translate spacings between equipotentials into a field profile.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Reading field strength from potential instead of its gradient

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must recognise three standard current–voltage characteristics.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Confusing diode turn-on with filament heating

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must trace current through ideal meters and follow potential differences around the circuit.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Counting other branches in the ammeter reading

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must infer the balancing force and apply Fleming’s left-hand rule to the perspective drawing.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Reversing the field direction across the gap

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must follow the component of velocity perpendicular to the field through three stages.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Using the total speed in the motional e.m.f. formula

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must convert the first voltage to r.m.s., infer one resistance, and use the series total.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must step up the voltage, calculate the load current, and apply the transformer current ratio.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The student must calculate two particle rates and convert photon energy to joules.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Using current directly as a particle rate

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must convert position confinement to a momentum and then velocity uncertainty scale.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Leaving the confinement length in millimetres

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must translate the Rutherford scattering result into an angular count-rate graph.

asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must justify constant activity over two days and convert the duration to seconds.
asrjc-2022-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Using becquerels with a duration in days

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The calculation is short once a plausible speed and acceleration time are chosen.
asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q1.misconception: Using an unrealistic scale for everyday acceleration

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must propagate uncertainties through two differences and then through a quotient.

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must use the total distance to infer the duration of the acceleration phase.
asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Using total race time as acceleration time

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student needs to recognise a nonzero constant slope as terminal velocity.

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish the applied force from the resultant force on X and use Newton’s third law.
asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Treating the applied force as the resultant on X

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must interpret the magnitude of a negative momentum gradient as a force magnitude.

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student combines force directions and relative arrow lengths with the condition for constant velocity.
asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Assuming upward motion requires a net upward force

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must combine the wall’s normal force and friction while keeping the ground reaction vertical.
asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q8.misconception: Adding a friction component at a frictionless contact

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student only needs to identify the useful output and total input in the efficiency formula.

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must track the jumper’s height, speed and cord extension at each stage.
asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q10.misconception: Equating zero net force with zero speed

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The calculation requires one revolution in radians and conversion of 12 hours into seconds.

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The key step is using the separation of the two stars in the inverse-square law.
asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Using an orbital radius as the separation

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must compare two inverse-radius expressions and account for the negative sign of potential energy.
asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Treating gravitational potential energy as positive

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must use the phase of the velocity and account for the doubled frequency of kinetic energy.
asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q16.misconception: Using displacement squared for kinetic energy

asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must check both the shape of the response and its zero-frequency limit.
asrjc-2023-promo-p1-q17.misconception: Assuming damping reduces the static amplitude

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing a single disturbance from periodic driving.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Requires applying the definition of amplitude to the two rows.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Confusing particle spacing with particle displacement.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires finding the wavelength and identifying the second destructive-interference condition.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Using a whole-wavelength path difference for a dark fringe.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the allowed harmonics for a tube with a node at one end and an antinode at the other.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Treating a node–antinode tube as supporting every integer harmonic.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Requires finding carrier density first and applying it to a wire with a different cross-sectional area.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Scaling drift speed by radius instead of cross-sectional area.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Requires translating resistance per unit length into the slope of a potential graph.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Assuming the thickest wire has the steepest potential gradient.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires recognising the common central node before reducing the resistor network.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Counting resistors without identifying which nodes they connect.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Requires checking how heating changes the divider output and whether the diode can conduct.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Taking the divider output across the thermistor for a high-temperature alarm.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Requires reading the tangent to the field line and reversing the direction for an electron.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Using the electric field direction as the force direction on a negative charge.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires combining signed potentials and relating their gradient to the signed axial field.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Assuming the field vanishes where the potential is zero.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Requires applying the right-hand grip rule at four positions and summing the field vectors.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Adding field directions without resolving their components.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Requires linking the inverse-distance field to an increasing rate of flux change.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming constant wire speed implies constant induced current.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires using the gradient of a distance–time graph to infer the motional e.m.f.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Reading the distance itself as proportional to the e.m.f.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Requires comparing a half-wave rectified sine with a half-duty rectangular pulse.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Halving the peak to get the mean of a half-wave rectified sine.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Requires finding the largest accessible energy drop and relating it to photon wavelength.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Using an excited level above the incident electron energy.

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must connect the accelerating voltage to momentum before taking the wavelength ratio.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Treating wavelength as inversely proportional to voltage

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must compare rest masses and convert the mass difference to an energy threshold.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Confusing binding energy with energy released during breakup

asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must add the proton-number changes associated with successive emissions.
asrjc-2024-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Reversing the proton-number change in beta-minus decay

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The student needs a plausible car mass and one substitution into the kinetic-energy formula.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish a consistent offset from scatter about a straight line.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Confusing a nonzero intercept with random scatter

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must use the square of the time ratio for free fall from rest.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Assuming distance is proportional to time

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must identify the air and water sections and interpret both their slopes and areas.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Confusing height or duration with area on a velocity–time graph

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must identify the interaction and the body on which each force acts.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Pairing forces that balance on the same object

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must convert the flow rate and use the rate of change of momentum as a force.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Using mass per minute as mass per second

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must infer the rod angle and find three perpendicular moment arms before balancing torques.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Using along-rod distances as perpendicular moment arms

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must estimate the areas under both curves and take their difference.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Treating energy lost in hysteresis as recoverable elastic energy

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must combine constant acceleration from rest with the expression for instantaneous power.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming constant force gives constant power

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must combine inward acceleration with acceleration along the direction of motion.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Assuming acceleration in circular motion is always entirely centripetal

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must keep mass fixed and multiply weight by the field-strength ratio.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Treating mass as dependent on local gravity

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must replace mass per volume with density and take the square root after rearranging.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Confusing mean square speed with root-mean-square speed

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: It requires finding the compression work and applying the first law over a closed cycle.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Confusing work done on the gas with work done by the gas.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must identify the equilibrium position and invert the SHM displacement equation.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming equal distances take equal times in SHM.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: It links intensity to particle amplitude and distinguishes particle speed from wave speed.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Confusing particle speed with wave speed.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: It requires combining the source phase difference with the phase difference caused by the paths.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Ignoring the initial phase difference between the sources.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Matching the screen positions lets the student equate the order–wavelength products.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Assuming wavelength increases with order at a fixed diffraction angle.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must connect constant electric acceleration to a linear kinetic-energy graph.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Assuming constant acceleration makes kinetic energy quadratic in distance.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: It requires rearranging the definitions of potential difference, current and power.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Confusing the reciprocal of current with resistance.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: It requires tracing the extra parallel path and relating total current to the internal voltage drop.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Treating terminal potential difference as fixed when current changes.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: It requires identifying the correct potential divider inside a branched circuit.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Including a parallel resistor in the potential-divider ratio.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: It requires finding the wire’s potential gradient before applying the galvanometer balance condition.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Using the driving cell’s e.m.f. as the full wire voltage.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: It requires recognising the field at a solenoid end from the shape and direction of the lines.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Confusing axial magnetic fields with the circular field of a straight wire.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: It requires resolving the wire length perpendicular to the field and applying Fleming’s left-hand rule.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Using the angle to the normal directly in the sine form of the force equation.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: It requires tracking the rate of change of overlap area and the reversal of current at exit.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Using the flux itself to predict the induced current.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: It requires reading the time at each level and weighting the squared currents over a period.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Using the sinusoidal RMS formula for a non-sinusoidal waveform.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: It uses a standard photon-energy equation but requires estimating the frequency of violet light.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Misjudging the photon energy scale for visible light.

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Finds a new uncertainty bound and compares it with the initial value.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Assuming the initial uncertainty is minimal

asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Tracks proton and nucleon numbers through three emissions.
asrjc-2025-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Confusing proton number with nucleon number

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing random/systematic errors and the effect of timing many oscillations.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Confusing random and systematic errors and what each technique reduces

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Needs reasoning about the range of resultant magnitudes for two vectors at an angle.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Thinking the resultant always exceeds the larger force or forgetting angle dependence

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Combines time of fall with relative horizontal velocity of a moving target.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Ignoring the target's motion or adding the velocities instead of subtracting

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Requires careful free-body reasoning for stacked blocks at rest and accelerating, and correct identification of third-law pairs.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Misidentifying Newton's third-law pairs and ignoring that acceleration changes contact forces

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Needs relative speed of approach = separation with a massive moving foot.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Assuming the foot must move towards the ball to stop it

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Sum of four equal moments for rotational equilibrium.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Counting only one or two carriages

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Recognise constant $E_k$ and linear decrease of $E_p$ at terminal velocity.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Assuming kinetic energy increases as potential energy is lost even at terminal velocity

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Two-step efficiency calculation using useful light power.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Confusing heat output percentage with efficiency

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Combine energy conservation for speed with Newton's second law for circular motion.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Taking tension at the lowest point to equal the weight

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Vector addition of fields in opposite directions plus scalar addition of potentials.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Treating field strength as a scalar sum or potential as a vector that cancels

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Qualitative first-law reasoning about a sudden (adiabatic) compression.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Assuming temperature stays constant because pV is constant or the container is insulated

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Requires reading the cycle area on a p-V graph and deciding the sign from the clockwise direction.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Confusing work done by the gas with work done on the gas; mishandling powers of ten

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Assuming speed varies linearly with displacement

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Requires linking compressions/rarefactions in a progressive longitudinal wave to pressure and particle velocity.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Applying standing-wave terms (nodes, antinodes) to a progressive wave; thinking molecules at a rarefaction are at rest

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Needs to find the fundamental of the open tube and convert to the closed-tube harmonic series.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Assuming closed tubes support all harmonics, or that closing an end raises frequency

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Requires finding $d/\lambda$ from the given order and then the maximum integer with $\sin\theta \le 1$.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Rounding up the maximum order or assuming 90° gives a visible order

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: One-step use of $Q = It$ and $N = Q/e$.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Forgetting to convert mA or to divide by the electron charge

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Two simultaneous equations from $E = I(R + r)$.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Ignoring internal resistance or using $R = V/I$ for the external circuit only

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Combining series and parallel capacitors and sharing charge between parallel branches.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Assuming charge is shared equally between parallel branches, or that every capacitor has the same charge

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Requires recognising that energy decays with time constant $RC/2$ because $E \propto V^2$.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Applying the exponential decay of V or Q directly to energy (forgetting the factor of 2)

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Must check both zero resultant force and zero resultant torque for four configurations.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Thinking zero net force alone guarantees equilibrium

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires deducing the field direction from the balance, then tracking energy changes for a positive charge.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Assuming electric and gravitational potential energy always change together or by equal amounts

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Requires 3D visualisation and applying the left-hand rule to negative charges.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Treating electrons as positive charges when applying the left-hand rule, or setting B parallel/antiparallel to E

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Qualitative application of Faraday's and Lenz's laws to reversed pole and lower speed.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Forgetting that reversing the pole reverses the induced current, or that the size depends on rate of change of flux

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires the force on charges in a moving conductor and the source-versus-load sign of potential.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Assuming current flows from high to low potential inside the source (the disc) as it does in the external resistor

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Must read the full 4 s period (including the zero interval) and average $I^2R$ rather than $I$.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Averaging the current (which gives zero net charge) instead of the power, or missing the zero-current interval

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Direct recall of the de Broglie relation $\lambda = h/p$.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Confusing which particle property the de Broglie wavelength depends on, or inverting the relationship

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Links the spread of $|\psi|^2$ to $\Delta x$ and applies the uncertainty principle qualitatively.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Thinking a sharply peaked (well-localised) wavefunction means well-defined momentum

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Tracking the neutron number change for each decay type.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Thinking β-decay leaves the neutron number unchanged or that γ emission changes the nucleus composition

asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Requires separating the constant background from the decaying source count over two half-lives.
asrjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Halving the total count rate, including background, each half-life

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Converts a percentage uncertainty and rounds the reading to match.

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Uses two elapsed times in the displacement equations and solves for catch-up.

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Identifies the effect of gravity on each velocity component.

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Uses opposite signs for the initial velocities in one momentum equation.

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Tracks a velocity reversal and distinguishes net impulse from contact impulse.
cjc-2022-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Confusing net impulse with contact impulse

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Uses the extension and accounts for the increasing spring force.
cjc-2022-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Using the full length as the extension

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Applies floating equilibrium and Archimedes' principle to different states.

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Balances moments twice as both lever arms change.

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Combines force balance with the additional speed factor in power.

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Tracks the sign and magnitude of the work gradient.

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Distinguishes a vector's constant magnitude from its changing direction.
cjc-2022-promo-p1-q11.misconception: Confusing acceleration magnitude with its change

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Identifies which quantities depend on satellite mass.
cjc-2022-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Assuming equal speeds imply equal kinetic energies

cjc-2022-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Uses the initial phase to find successive zeroes of displacement.
cjc-2022-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Using the wrong release phase or crossing interval

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Single application of the rule for combining percentage uncertainties with a power.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Forgetting to multiply the uncertainty of a squared quantity by its power

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Needs vector subtraction for relative velocity, a common slip in direction.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Adding velocities instead of subtracting, or finding Q relative to P

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires treating the hole as negative mass and taking a weighted average of centres.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Ignoring the removed area or measuring the hole position from the wrong edge

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Combines F = BIL with N turns and a principle-of-moments calculation using the correct perpendicular distances.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Using the wrong perpendicular distances or forgetting that only the bottom side is in the field

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Direct link between constant force, constant acceleration and a linear velocity rise.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Thinking velocity follows the force, or that the body stops when the force is removed

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: One application of F = ma with resistive force included.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Forgetting the resistive force or using only ma

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Two-step: useful power from P = Fv, then input power from energy per minute.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Forgetting to convert energy per minute into power

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Requires recognising the ball still has horizontal KE at the top and estimating its fraction.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Thinking KE is zero at the top of the trajectory

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Direct use of relative speed of approach equals relative speed of separation.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming the masses are equal, or that P must stop or keep going forward

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Straight substitution into a = rω² with ω = 2π/T and a unit conversion.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Forgetting the cm to m conversion or omitting 2π

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Requires knowing field lines are perpendicular to equipotentials and point to lower potential.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Thinking the field points towards higher (less negative) potential

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Uses φ ∝ 1/r and the fact that the field weakens with distance.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Thinking potential difference stays the same for a fixed separation, as in a uniform field

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Needs phase reasoning from a to x to v and recognising KE has half the period.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Forgetting that kinetic energy oscillates at twice the frequency of displacement

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Needs timing of travel to and from the fixed end plus the phase inversion on reflection.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Forgetting that a pulse reflected at a fixed end is inverted, or reversing the order of its parts

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Combines intensity proportional to source power and inverse-square distance.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Applying only one of the two changes, or using 1/r instead of 1/r²

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Needs to halve the 60° angle before using d sinθ = nλ and to convert to lines per mm.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Using the full angle between orders instead of the angle from the normal

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Needs the Rayleigh criterion with an estimated visible wavelength.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Using a wrong wavelength order of magnitude for visible light

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Uses ΔU as a state function across two paths with careful sign convention.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Thinking heat transfer is the same for both paths, or mixing up sign conventions

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Simple heat balance where c cancels and mass is proportional to volume.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Swapping which mass goes with which temperature

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Requires scaling E with Q/r² and combining field directions correctly.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Subtracting the fields because the charges have opposite signs

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Single application of $I = nAvq$ with two ratio changes.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Forgetting that area scales with diameter squared

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Potential divider reasoning with standard NTC and LDR behaviour.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Thinking resistance of an NTC thermistor rises with temperature

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Needs to identify series/parallel arrangement then combine capacitances and use $Q = CV$.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Treating all capacitors as in parallel, or charge as the sum on each capacitor

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Combines r.m.s.-to-peak conversion with the $\sin^2$ shape of power.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Using the r.m.s. current as the peak, or a $|\sin|$ shape for power

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires 3D direction reasoning for both forces on a negative charge across four field combinations.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Assuming E and B must always be perpendicular for undeflected motion

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Direct use of flux cut $= BLvt$ with unit conversions.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Forgetting to convert minutes to seconds or cm to m

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Linking intensity to photon energy or wave amplitude

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Requires understanding which position and momentum components the slit constrains.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Taking $\Delta p$ along the direction of travel or $\Delta y$ at the screen

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Applies $\beta^-$ decay changes to a nuclide chart.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Swapping proton and neutron changes in beta decay

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Direct recall of the Rutherford scattering interpretation.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The shared angular speed cancels in a direct centripetal-force ratio.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Assuming the masses share a linear speed.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The inverse-square law must be combined with how mass scales at fixed density.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Holding mass fixed when the sphere grows.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The calculation requires the orbital radius and the period implied by geostationary motion.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Using altitude as the orbital radius.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must identify a half-cycle phase difference and match it to SHM variables.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Confusing a quarter-cycle phase shift with a half-cycle shift.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must combine the squared amplitude dependence with the inverse-square period dependence.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Scaling energy linearly with amplitude or period.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student converts frequency to period and reads the horizontal length of one cycle.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Using the whole display width for one period.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must translate a collinear arrangement into a path difference and test for a whole number of wavelengths.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Using one source-to-observer distance as the path difference.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish changes to the central maximum width from changes to the total transmitted light.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Assuming a wider slit transmits the same amount of light.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must combine constant horizontal velocity and uniform vertical acceleration to obtain a square law.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Treating deflection as proportional to horizontal travel.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The ladder requires alternating voltage and current calculations across two successive junctions.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Using the end-branch current for all the resistors.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The familiar filament-lamp characteristic must be interpreted with voltage on the vertical axis.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Keeping the usual current-on-vertical-axis curve after swapping axes.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The equal branch voltages make the current ratio the inverse of the resistance ratio.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Assigning the largest current to the largest resistance.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The calculation is direct once the angle between the current and the field is read in three dimensions.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Using the field’s angle to the horizontal as its angle to the current.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The right-hand grip rule identifies the region in which the two fields can cancel.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming parallel currents produce fields in the same direction everywhere.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must trace both half-cycles and compare the total series resistance in each direction.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Treating opposite diodes as a full-wave rectifier or as equal-resistance paths.

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Straightforward weighted sum of percentage uncertainties.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Forgetting to multiply by the powers

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Requires recognising that shifting the graph down changes both net area and absolute area.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Assuming distance is unchanged because the graph shapes are identical

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Area under a linear force–extension graph between two points.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Using $Fx$ instead of $\tfrac{1}{2}Fx$ for elastic energy

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Needs careful free-body analysis of separate bodies and Newton's laws.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Equating zero resultant force with being at rest

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Standard result that acceleration down a frictionless slope is independent of mass.

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Whole-system acceleration then Newton's second law on one block.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Taking the force on the 2.0 kg block as the applied force minus friction

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Single Newton's second law equation at the top of a vertical circle.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Adding weight to the centripetal force instead of subtracting

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Vector addition of three point-mass fields at the centroid of an equilateral triangle.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Combining two fields at 120° as if they were at 60° (getting $\sqrt{3}$)

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Scalar sum of potentials plus recognising potential has no direction.

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Ignoring the period change or not squaring ω

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Must halve for unpolarised light, then apply Malus' law twice using angle differences between successive axes.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using the absolute axis angles instead of the angle between successive polariser axes

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Two proportional reasoning steps: intensity proportional to amplitude squared, then power conserved over a smaller area.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Treating intensity as proportional to amplitude rather than amplitude squared

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Direct use of the Rayleigh criterion and small-angle geometry with large powers of ten.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Inverting the ratio (dividing distance by angle) or using radius instead of diameter

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming r.m.s. speed is proportional to temperature

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires recognising that connected containers share a common pressure, then comparing V/T.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Ignoring that the pressure is equal in connected containers, or mishandling the V/T ratio

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Needs an energy budget to decide that not all the ice melts, then compute the mass melted.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Assuming all ice melts or confusing 0 K with 0 °C

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Needs to combine $I = nAvq$ with $N = nAL$ so that the unknown area cancels.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Not realising the cross-sectional area cancels; using number density instead of total number

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Must combine the half-power rule for sinusoidal a.c. with the effect of half-wave rectification.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Ignoring that the diode blocks half of each cycle

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Parallel combination plus internal resistance; routine calculation.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Forgetting the internal resistance or adding the resistors in series

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Must trace each circuit to find the potential range between X and Y as the slider moves.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Assuming any potentiometer arrangement gives a range starting from zero

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Must identify the series pair across the battery and share the voltage inversely with capacitance.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Sharing voltage in proportion to capacitance rather than inversely

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires two ideas: equal and opposite forces (Newton's third law) and attraction for parallel currents.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Thinking the wire with larger current exerts or feels a larger force

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Chained calculation: field, acceleration, time in plates, then deflection, plus direction reasoning.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Using the plate separation as the distance travelled or reversing the force direction for a positive charge

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Coulomb's law ratio with a small trap in reading 'adding 3Q'.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Reading 'adding 3Q' as making the charge 3Q, or forgetting to square the distance

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Simple recognition that the field is unchanged while the perpendicular area decreases.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Confusing magnetic flux density with magnetic flux

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Direct application of Faraday's law with flux linkage.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Forgetting to multiply by the number of turns

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Recall $E = hc/\lambda$ and recognise the linear graph against $1/\lambda$.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Thinking photon energy increases with wavelength

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Forgetting to square the well width

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Unfamiliar twist: mass lost is only the escaping alpha particles, not the decayed nuclei.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Equating the mass lost with the fraction of nuclei decayed

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Recall of penetrating power of alpha, beta and gamma radiation.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Mixing up the penetrating abilities of alpha, beta and gamma

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Standard base-unit derivation via $V = W/Q$ with $Q = It$.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Treating derived units such as the ohm or coulomb as SI base units

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Requires reading gradient and sign of a v–t graph rather than any calculation.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Confusing zero acceleration with change of direction

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Two applications of Newton's second law with a changing mass and careful sign handling.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Ignoring direction of acceleration or forgetting the mass changes in the second case

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Single moments equation about one end plus force balance.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Inverting the ratio or neglecting the plank's weight

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Direct Hooke's law with extension computed from lengths.

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Equating elastic energy stored to gravitational energy lost by the mass

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Energy bookkeeping with work, friction and GPE on an incline.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Using the distance along the slope as the vertical height gain

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: One-step use of $v = r\omega$ with common angular velocity.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Thinking points at different radii on a rigid disc have different periods

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Counter-intuitive result that losing energy increases orbital speed.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming that losing energy to drag makes the satellite slower

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Ratio reasoning with $g \propto 1/r^2$ and $\phi \propto 1/r$, with the height-vs-distance trap.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using height above the surface (3R) instead of distance from Earth's centre (4R)
