jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Same temperature means same mean KE, giving $v_{rms} \propto 1/\sqrt{m}$.

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Combines specific heat and latent heat then divides by power.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Including only one of the two energy stages

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Ideal gas law at constant volume with changing mass and kelvin conversion.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Using Celsius instead of kelvin temperatures

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Must combine $a_0 = \omega^2x_0$ and $E = \tfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2x_0^2$ with three ratios.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming the same angular frequency for both bodies

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires choosing the cosine form and solving for phase, not assuming linear motion.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Assuming the bob moves at constant speed so half the distance takes half the time

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Malus' law with the halving at the first polariser and a percentage decrease to interpret.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Forgetting the first polariser halves unpolarised light, or using cos instead of cos²

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Standard comparison of open–open and closed–open pipe fundamentals.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Mixing up which pipe type has the longer fundamental wavelength

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Must estimate the wavelength of visible light and apply the Rayleigh criterion.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Using the aperture size directly or a wrong order of magnitude for light's wavelength

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Must deduce the fixed charge is $-e$, then superpose potentials of opposite sign.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Ignoring the alpha particle's own potential or adding magnitudes regardless of sign

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Must recognise $v + V = E$ and locate the endpoints at $R = r$ and $R = 3r$.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Thinking the p.d. across the internal resistance rises with external resistance

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Requires redrawing a switched network into series and parallel blocks and comparing four configurations.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Closing a switch adds a parallel path, which lowers resistance

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Needs only $E = \tfrac12 CV^2$ and $mgh$ proportional to it.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Assuming energy stored is proportional to V rather than V²

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Needs $F = BIL\sin\theta$ with the right angle, plus the idea that the magnetic force supplies half the weight.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Using cos θ instead of sin θ, or equating the magnetic force to the full weight

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Two standard relations (accelerating p.d. and velocity selector) combined algebraically.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Forgetting to square v = E/B when substituting into the kinetic energy

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Students must see that the two arm e.m.f.s cancel, despite the motion graph pointing towards a velocity-shaped answer.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Treating the e.m.f. across PQ as proportional to the velocity of the wire

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Direct recall of how a transformer works.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Thinking a transformer passes current through a wire connection or works with d.c.

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Qualitative use of $\Delta y\,\Delta p_y \gtrsim h$ in a standard single-slit context.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Thinking a narrower slit gives a more focused beam

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Recall of electron diffraction plus the link $\lambda = h/(mv)$.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Attributing electron rings to repulsion, or getting the λ–speed trend backwards

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Read a data table against known penetrating powers, allowing for background.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Forgetting to subtract background, so the 301 count with lead looks like gamma

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Needs the ratio converted to $N_0/N$ before applying exponential decay with the half-life.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Treating the daughter-to-parent ratio as the fraction decayed or as the fraction remaining

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Homogeneity check: $\tan\alpha$ is dimensionless, so each term must be too.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Thinking angles in degrees give Q a unit

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Standard terminal-velocity reasoning applied to an acceleration–time graph.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Thinking acceleration levels off at a non-zero value, or confusing a–t with v–t

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Distinguishing kinetic energy conservation overall from what happens during the contact.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Believing kinetic energy is conserved at every instant during an elastic collision

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Needs two Newton's second law equations with the acceleration ratio, then solving simultaneously.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Ignoring friction in one case or doubling the gravity component too

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Needs the upthrust held fixed while the centre of gravity shifts, then the sense of the couple.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Assuming upthrust drops along with the weight

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Needs a force balance on a slope, noting that gravity helps drive the car downhill, before using $P = Fv$.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Ignoring the component of weight along the slope

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Simple efficiency, work and power substitution.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Applying efficiency in the wrong direction or treating weight as mass

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Standard vertical-circle force balance at the top.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Treating tension as the only centripetal force or getting the sign of weight wrong

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Inverse-square ratio, with the trap of using height rather than distance from the centre.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Using height above the surface instead of distance from the centre, or thinking orbiting objects are weightless

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Relating loss of PE to work done by the field and the field direction.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Confusing force (E/x) with field strength (E/mx), or reversing the field direction

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Single substitution into the mean KE formula after converting to kelvin; the moles and molar mass are red herrings.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using Celsius temperature or computing the total kinetic energy of the gas instead of per atom

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Requires recognising equal pressure in connected flasks and combining the volume and temperature ratios.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Ignoring that the connected flasks share the same pressure, or inverting the temperature dependence

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Standard conceptual check of internal energy and the first law.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Equating internal energy with temperature, or treating heat and work as stored quantities

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Resonance condition plus a single speed = distance × frequency step.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Dividing frequency by spacing (or spacing by frequency) instead of multiplying

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires knowing that damping lowers the oscillation frequency, which students often ignore for light damping.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Believing damping has no effect on the period, or that the period changes as amplitude decays

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Malus' law with an inverse cosine and the extra step of finding an equivalent angle beyond 180°.

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Needs $I \propto A^2$ and reading amplitudes off grids while noticing frequency is unchanged.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Thinking amplitude halves when intensity halves, or that frequency changes with intensity

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Direct Rayleigh criterion with a small-angle conversion to separation.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Applying the diffraction angle without multiplying by the object distance, or using radius instead of aperture width

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires vector addition of four fields with careful attention to direction for each charge sign.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Adding field magnitudes without direction, or thinking all like charges give the largest field

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Needs adapting $I = nAvq$ to charge per unit length rather than recall.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Treating I/e (protons per second) as protons per unit length

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Combines potential-divider reasoning with thermistor behaviour and diode orientation.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Placing the thermistor in the wrong arm of the potential divider or ignoring diode direction

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Chains $I = Q/t$, $V = W/Q$ and the e.m.f. equation, with a minutes-to-seconds conversion.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Not converting minutes to seconds, or confusing R with r

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Standard derivation of the cyclotron period that students often memorise.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Assuming a faster particle takes less time to complete the circle

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Requires finding acceleration from $eE/m$ then applying uniform-acceleration kinematics.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Using force instead of acceleration in the kinematics equation

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Simple $P \propto I^2$ scaling once the r.m.s. idea is understood.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Thinking power scales linearly with current, or applying the sinusoidal factor $\sqrt{2}$

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: One-step use of $\lambda = h/(mv)$ comparing masses.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Associating the lightest particle with the smallest velocity

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Combines photon momentum with rate of change of momentum, including the factor of 2 on reflection.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Forgetting the factor of 2 for reflection, or using $p = h\lambda$

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Tests several subtle points: binding energy vs per nucleon, mass-energy in reactions, momentum conservation and decay independence.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Judging nuclear stability by total binding energy rather than binding energy per nucleon

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Needs total binding energies (BE per nucleon × A) and their difference, not a difference of per-nucleon values.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Subtracting binding energies per nucleon instead of total binding energies

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Rearranging the fractional-uncertainty sum with the power of 2 on t.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Forgetting to double the percentage uncertainty in t, or adding instead of subtracting

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Single order-of-magnitude estimate from everyday knowledge.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Poor sense of scale when converting cm to m³

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: One resolution of weight along the slope set equal to the given maximum friction.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Using cosine instead of sine for the component along the slope

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Requires the perpendicular distance from O to side BA in a regular hexagon.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Taking the distance OB instead of the perpendicular distance to the line of action

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Best solved by noticing both masses share the same acceleration, so relative motion is uniform.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Thinking the accelerations make the relative motion non-uniform

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Needs recognising that equal time intervals require heights in the ratio 1:4:9:16.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Assuming equally spaced beads give equally spaced sounds

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Efficiency then P = Fv with constant velocity.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Using input power instead of useful output power

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Qualitative use of $F = mr\omega^2$ with friction providing the centripetal force.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Thinking objects further out have a larger angular velocity

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Resolving tension for a conical pendulum and converting angular velocity to period.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Using the wrong trigonometric ratio when resolving tension

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Ratio of orbital speeds; main trap is measuring distance from the surface instead of the centre.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using distance from Earth's surface instead of from its centre

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using an inverse-square dependence on radius for potential

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Reading the gradient of an a–x graph and taking a square root.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Forgetting to square-root the gradient to get ω

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Needs particle direction from the wave's travel direction plus phase difference from the separation in wavelengths.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Getting the direction of particle motion wrong for a travelling wave

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Uses width ratio for distance, then inverse-square intensity and amplitude ∝ √I.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Thinking amplitude falls in the same proportion as intensity

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Compare fundamental frequencies of closed and open pipes, then check harmonics.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Treating open and closed pipes as having the same fundamental for the same length

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Requires using the longest wavelength to limit complete orders and counting both sides.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Using the shortest wavelength, or forgetting orders on both sides

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Needs conservation of total moles with equal final pressures and kelvin temperatures.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Using Celsius temperatures or assuming moles stay proportional to volume

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Eliminating the unknown heat loss with two simultaneous equations.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Ignoring heat loss to the surroundings

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Summing scalar potentials and multiplying by a negative charge with care over signs.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Sign error from forgetting the electron's negative charge

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Option D needs a vector sum of fields at Z before and after; the difference is small.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Assuming field strength at Z must decrease because one charge moves

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Turns ratio then Ohm's law and power with r.m.s. values.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Using the peak-power doubling or inverting the turns ratio

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: One substitution of Q = It into C = Q/V with prefix handling.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Prefix or power-of-ten slip with micro/milli

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Recognise two groups of three parallel capacitors joined in series.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Confusing series and parallel combination rules for capacitors

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Must realise the velocity selector fixes equal speeds, then use r = mv/(qB) as a ratio.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming the ions have equal kinetic energy or forgetting both mass and charge change

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Combines F = BIL to find BL, SHM maximum speed, and motional e.m.f. BLv.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Using amplitude or frequency directly as the speed instead of v0 = ωx0

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Needs E0 = NBAω so doubling frequency doubles both peak e.m.f. and frequency.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Thinking only the frequency changes and the peak e.m.f. stays the same

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Standard photoelectric fact: intensity affects photon rate only.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Believing light intensity changes the threshold frequency or electron energy

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Convert both wavelengths to photon energies and compare against two work functions in an unfamiliar electroscope setup.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Thinking shorter wavelength light always causes emission regardless of work function

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Requires knowing that the closer alpha particle feels greater repulsion and is deflected more.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Thinking alpha particles are attracted to the nucleus or that farther particles deflect more

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Must read P's half-life directly and find D1's half-life from its tail after P has decayed.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Reading D1's half-life from its peak or from the start rather than its exponential tail

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Single rearrangement of SI base units.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Forgetting that angular speed has unit $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ or misexpressing the joule

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Compare fractional uncertainties with the power of D, and ignore the irrelevant R.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Comparing absolute instead of fractional uncertainties, or including irrelevant data

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Must use extensions from natural length, not the change in length directly.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Using the 10 mm change in length as the extension

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Tests precise conditions for equilibrium and properties of a couple.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Believing zero resultant force alone guarantees equilibrium

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Must deduce the sign convention (downward positive) from the graph before judging each statement.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Assuming upward is positive and so misreading which point is the maximum upward velocity

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Must model mass flow rate ρAv and the rate of KE transfer, with area from diameter.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Using radius-diameter confusion or forgetting the ½ in kinetic energy

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Interpret area under a force–displacement graph as work done by each force.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Confusing the gain in kinetic energy (P) with the energy dissipated

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Two-step ratio: fall time scales with the square root of height.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Assuming horizontal distance is proportional to the drop height

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Uses Newton's third law to get the force on Y from X's momentum change.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Using the speed change of Y without knowing its final velocity, or ignoring direction

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Must bound v using energy conservation: enough to rise above the centre but not enough to complete the loop.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Thinking v = √(gr) at the bottom is the condition for completing the loop

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Direct use of Kepler's third law with a ratio.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Assuming period is proportional to radius

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Direct recall of the defining features of a geostationary orbit.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Thinking orbital radius depends on the satellite's mass

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Needs linking x = 0 at t = 0 to maximum KE and recognising KE never goes negative and has twice the frequency.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Plotting KE with the same shape and frequency as displacement

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Requires reading displacements off a longitudinal-particle diagram and deducing particle velocity from wave direction.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Confusing compression/rarefaction position with direction of particle motion

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Standard crest/trough reading of a two-source wavefront diagram.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Thinking the gap between wavefronts (trough-trough) gives cancellation

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Needs computing angular separation and aperture from Rayleigh criterion, then checking each statement.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Thinking a longer wavelength improves resolution

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Direct recall of the kinetic theory assumptions.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Believing all gas molecules have the same speed

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Needs recognising zero net change in U over a cycle, finding enclosed area and its sign, then applying the first law.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Getting the sign of work done on the gas wrong for a clockwise cycle

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Needs scalar superposition of potentials and the sign convention for work done by the field.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Confusing work done by the field with work done by an external agent

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Single Coulomb's-law substitution, with care over the pico prefix and alpha charge.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Using the electron charge for the alpha particle or mis-converting pm

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Requires recognising that current flows radially, so the depth sets the cross-sectional area, not the length.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Taking the liquid depth as the conductor length

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Needs reasoning about where potential difference appears across a break in a series circuit.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Thinking a voltmeter across a broken component reads zero

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Mixing up the series and parallel rules for capacitors

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Needs fields from two wires and recognising the two contributions are perpendicular.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Adding or subtracting the two fields as if parallel

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Needs applying Lenz's law to eddy currents in an unfamiliar set-up.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Expecting no interaction because aluminium is non-magnetic

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Chains transformer power, peak-to-r.m.s. conversion and $I^2R$ loss.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Using the peak voltage instead of the r.m.s. voltage

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Needs realising photon momentum and photon rate both depend on wavelength and cancel.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Thinking pressure depends on photon momentum alone, not the photon rate

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Direct recall of the probabilistic interpretation of the wavefunction.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Picturing the electron as following a definite orbit

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Needs normalising activity per gram before applying exponential decay.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Comparing activities without scaling for sample mass

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Needs energy release as the increase in total binding energy, counting nucleons correctly.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Including free neutrons in the product binding energy

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Direct application of the definitions of systematic and random error to a distribution.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Confusing systematic error (offset) with random error (spread)

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: A routine application of the rule for combining percentage uncertainties.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Subtracting uncertainties for quantities in the denominator

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Students must apply the three-forces-concurrent condition and account for friction at both contact surfaces.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Assuming the wall force is purely horizontal (normal only) even on a rough wall

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Students must link the thrust to the rate of change of momentum of the air and share the weight among four propellers.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Forgetting to share the weight among the four propellers

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: This needs a direct link from balanced forces to constant speed and a linear loss of $E_p$.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Assuming gravitational potential energy is always converted into kinetic energy during a fall

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Students must recognise that the ball inherits the upward velocity and then solve a quadratic for the time.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Ignoring the initial upward velocity inherited from the moving balloon

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Students must identify the common velocity at maximum compression and combine momentum with energy conservation.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Not realising that the blocks share a common velocity at maximum compression

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Students must resolve the tension in two directions, use the right radius and eliminate the unknown angle.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Taking the string length as the radius of the circular path

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: A simple proportionality argument once friction is identified as the centripetal force.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming the maximum speed is proportional to the friction force

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: A standard null-point problem with a simple square root.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Forgetting to take the square root of the mass ratio

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: A direct use of $\phi = -GM/r$, but sign handling trips up some students.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Sign errors when subtracting negative potentials

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Students must convert scale readings into displacements from equilibrium and solve two inverse-cosine equations.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Measuring displacement from the end of the scale rather than from equilibrium

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Students must read $x_0$ and $v_0$ from the ellipse and realise that constant energy forces $\omega$ to change.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Assuming the angular frequency stays the same when the amplitude changes

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Students must read the wavelength from a particle-position diagram and recall basic wave properties.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Taking compression-to-rarefaction distance as a full wavelength

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Students must halve the angle, find $d/\lambda$ and then count the orders on both sides plus the central maximum.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Using 56° rather than 28° as the diffraction angle, or forgetting the central maximum

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Students must choose a visible wavelength themselves and combine the Rayleigh criterion with the small-angle approximation.

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: A direct ratio calculation from the mean kinetic energy formula.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Forgetting to square the r.m.s. speed ratio

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Straightforward use of the first law, with care over sign conventions.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Confusing heat supplied to the gas with heat lost by the gas

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires $V \propto d^3$ and using the change in volume for the work done.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Using final volume instead of change in volume for work done

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Students must read the distances off a grid (including diagonals) and apply the inverse square law.

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: A standard result, though students often confuse zero field with zero potential.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Zero electric field inside implies zero potential inside

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Combines the current and resistance equations and cancels area.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Assuming radius affects drift speed at fixed voltage

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the active loop and accounting for the internal voltage drop.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Assuming a charged capacitor opens every loop

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Requires finding the initial current and recalculating the signed net force at half that current.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Halving net force when only magnetic force halves

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires visualizing the rotated wire and adding two perpendicular field vectors.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Adding field magnitudes without checking directions

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Applies the ideal transformer turns ratio at fixed input voltage.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Treating load resistance as a control for ideal secondary voltage

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Requires rearranging the energy equation and forming a ratio involving three quantities.

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Requires recalling the atomic length scale and using it to estimate the momentum uncertainty.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Using a nuclear length scale for an atom

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Requires isolating two source rates, decaying them separately and restoring the background.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Applying radioactive decay to background counts

ri-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Requires calculating total binding energies and allocating the released energy to kinetic energy and the photon.
ri-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Equating total released energy to photon energy

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Requires deriving the mass and propagating uncertainties through a subtraction and a division.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Treating relative uncertainty as absolute uncertainty

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Requires identifying which weights each spring supports before applying Hooke's law.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Assuming identical tension in both springs

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires applying the momentum-rate form of Newton's second law to incoming rain at constant car speed.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Assuming constant car speed means the collected rain requires no force

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Requires opposite velocity signs in a direct impulse calculation.

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Requires using force balance to find the speed ratio and then using the power relation.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Assuming power scales directly with thrust as speed changes

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Requires relating horizontal displacement and vertical rise over the same time and using trajectory symmetry.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Using the displacement to the apex as the full range

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Requires matching three graphs by their initial values, slopes and terminal behavior.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Treating zero net force as zero speed

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Requires comparing the impulses delivered by gravity and the floor over the short contact time.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Assuming gravity stops acting during contact

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Requires solving simultaneous signed momentum and relative-speed equations.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Assigning the other trolley's velocity to P

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Requires comparing gas states at equal pressure and converting both temperatures to kelvin.

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Requires using the first law to connect rapid compression with a temperature rise.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Confusing work on the gas with heat from the surroundings

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Recognising uniform speed is enough to test the statement about resultant force.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Confusing the rod force with the resultant force

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Use the orbital period–radius scaling and convert days to hours.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Using the wrong power of orbital radius

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Identify both distances from the Moon’s centre and apply conservation of energy.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Using height in place of distance from the centre

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Read the positions of equilibrium and the turning points from the graph.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Taking the peak-to-peak distance as the amplitude

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Substitute the total energy into the kinetic energy expression and solve for displacement.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Treating energy as linear in displacement

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Identify the standard phase, spacing and amplitude properties of a stationary wave.

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Apply different resonance conditions to open and closed pipes.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Applying the same resonance condition to both pipe types

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Add the signed potential energies of both charge pairs and then conserve energy.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Losing the sign or factor of two in the kinetic energy change

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Check both the angle of the field lines at the plates and how their spacing changes.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Drawing field lines that meet conductors obliquely

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Compare the mean squares of two waveforms over a full cycle before equating the powers.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Using the full sine-wave RMS factor for a half-wave rectified sine

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Identify the three circuit nodes and reduce the redrawn network.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Reading the physical layout as a series connection

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Determine which side permits cancellation and use the two different distances in the field equation.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Equating field magnitudes where both fields point the same way

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Compare the curvature of particle paths using the mass-to-charge ratio.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Comparing charge alone to predict deflection

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Compare how fast the flux changes at each stage in the two-coil circuit.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Equating the largest primary current with the largest induced current

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Combine Faraday’s law with the current–charge relation and include both resistances.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Using only the coil resistance or mis-converting square centimetres

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Use the inverse relationship and keep the order of the ratio straight.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Treating the two uncertainties as directly proportional

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Express momentum in terms of kinetic energy before substituting into the de Broglie equation.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Inverting the de Broglie relation or dropping the kinetic energy factor of one half

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Distinguish the inferences from scattering data from claims about nuclear composition.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Inferring neutrons directly from Rutherford scattering

rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Track both proton and nucleon numbers across the three successive decays.
rvhs-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Tracking the alpha decay without both beta decays

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Express tension and linear mass density in base units and equate the exponents.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Using mass instead of mass per unit length

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Requires rearranging familiar field equations and converting derived units.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Confusing magnetic flux with magnetic flux density

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires applying Newton’s second law to the pair and then to one block.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Applying the full pulling force to Y alone

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Requires reading a triangular area as net work and equating it to the gain in kinetic energy.

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Requires adding the initial energies and subtracting a single friction loss.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Adding dissipated energy to kinetic energy

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Requires resolving weight along the slope, converting force into power and adding the original engine power.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Confusing additional power with total power

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Requires recognising that the separation grows with the square of time for two cars starting from rest.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Assuming separation grows linearly with time

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Requires comparing the signs and relative sizes of velocity gradients through four stages.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Reading acceleration from the height of a velocity graph

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Requires writing separate radial force equations at the top and bottom before subtracting.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Equating tension with centripetal force everywhere

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing the distance between the stars from star b’s orbital radius.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using the same radius for gravity and circular motion

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Requires identifying simple harmonic motion from the force graph and recognising the quadratic energy dependence.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Assuming any two curves with constant total energy fit SHM

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Requires finding the equilibrium crossings and reading the direction of motion there.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Confusing maximum displacement with maximum speed

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Requires comparing phase in a progressive wave with phase within and between standing-wave loops.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Applying progressive-wave phase rules within a standing-wave loop

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires using the final absolute temperature and distinguishing the escaped fraction from the remaining fraction.

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing the mechanical assumptions behind gas pressure from a later result about temperature.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Treating the temperature relation as an input to the pressure derivation

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Requires carrying the same internal-energy change across both paths and assigning the correct sign to work.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Treating work done by the gas as positive in Q + W

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Requires finding the electric force and subtracting weight before calculating acceleration.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Ignoring weight in the net force

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires tracking the motion of a negative charge and the associated energy transfer.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Assuming a negative charge moves toward lower potential

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Requires finding the period from angular speed and counting the charge that passes in one revolution.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Using orbital speed instead of revolution frequency

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing static resistance from the reciprocal slope of a straight line with a nonzero intercept.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Taking reciprocal I–V gradient as resistance

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires finding the potential of both midpoints before applying Ohm’s law to the connecting wire.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Using a supply voltage as the bridge voltage

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: It uses two short charge equations and a unit conversion.

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The two current products, separations and force directions must all be compared.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Ignoring force direction or wire separation

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: It combines Fleming’s left-hand rule with recognition that the angle to the field stays at a right angle.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Using the angle to the horizontal in the magnetic force formula

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: It requires distinguishing flux density from flux and flux linkage in a variable-area core.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Confusing flux density with flux linkage

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: It combines power conservation, rms values and the transformer voltage ratio.

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: It requires finding the highest accessible level and counting transitions between all accessible levels.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Counting only transitions to the ground state

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: It requires equating two decay laws with different half-lives and simplifying the powers.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Confusing elapsed time with the number of half-lives

sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: It requires scaling the binding energy per nucleon and identifying the direction of energy transfer.
sajc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Confusing binding energy per nucleon with total binding energy

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: It requires expressing energy in base units and simplifying the units of the rearranged equation.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Using degrees Celsius as an SI base unit

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: It requires estimating familiar lengths and converting them to volumes by powers of ten.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Using an atomic length directly as an atomic volume

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: It requires checking both force and torque balance separately for three configurations.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Equating zero resultant force with equilibrium

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: It requires resolving the sloping plane’s normal reaction and applying equilibrium in two directions.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: It requires reading the momentum gradient and using its sign in a force balance.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Confusing resultant force with an individual force

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: It requires linking the last second and the whole ascent through their shared endpoint at zero speed.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Assuming distance is proportional to time during the ascent

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: It requires comparing conserved energy separately from energy converted per unit time.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Confusing energy transferred with its rate of transfer

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: It requires finding the same tension from two force balances and using it to calculate power.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Adding the weights to compute the power delivered by the string

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: It requires obtaining the horizontal speed from the range and then calculating the kinetic energy at the apex.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming all velocity components vanish at the apex

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: It requires resolving the drag force and combining its vertical component with weight.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Applying the no-drag acceleration components when drag is present

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: It requires resolving momentum perpendicular to the cushion and accounting for its reversal.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Ignoring the sign reversal of the normal momentum

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: It requires applying both momentum and kinetic-energy conservation to interpret the result of a collision between equal masses.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Equating an elastic collision with equal and opposite outgoing velocities

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Students must identify which force provides the inward acceleration.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Friction must oppose the mass’s velocity.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Students must combine energy conservation, radial dynamics and Newton’s third law.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: The normal force equals the centripetal force.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Students must infer both the zero of the resultant force and its location.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Opposing gravitational forces cancel at the midpoint.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Students must distinguish changes in peak height, width and frequency.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Reducing damping shifts resonance to a lower frequency.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Students must use spherical spreading and convert the microphone area to square metres.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: A square-centimetre conversion uses the linear conversion factor.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Students must track the transmitted intensity and polarisation axis through three filters.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Malus’ law always uses the angle relative to the first filter.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Students must convert line density to spacing, bound the order and count both sides.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: The highest order equals the number of maxima.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Students must add the heat capacities and convert the required energy into a heating time.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Students must combine the ideal-gas law with the square-root dependence of rms speed on temperature.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Rms speed is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Students must distinguish the temperature dependence of kinetic energy from the mass dependence of speed.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Gas molecules at the same temperature have the same rms speed.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Students must convert the area and use the drift-current and resistance equations in sequence.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Square millimetres convert to square metres by a factor of $10^{-3}$.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Students must identify the measured resistor and infer the effect of increasing the LDR resistance.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: The voltmeter is across the LDR.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Students must scale the droplet’s volume and account for the reduced charge in the equilibrium equation.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Droplet mass scales linearly with radius.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Students must check both the crossing angles and the direction of decreasing potential.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Field lines can cross equipotentials obliquely.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Students must find each force direction and resolve the symmetric forces into components.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Magnetic force magnitudes on bent segments add directly.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Students must relate rim speed to rotation frequency and then to the flux swept per unit time.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Every point along the radius moves at the rim speed.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Students must convert the energy, calculate the momentum and apply the percentage uncertainty.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: The full momentum can be substituted for its uncertainty.

tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Students must convert binding energies per nucleon to total energies before finding the difference.
tjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Binding energies per nucleon can be subtracted directly to get the energy released.

tmjc-2023-other-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Two standard relations (turns ratio and $V^2/R$) combined algebraically.
tmjc-2023-other-p1-q25.misconception: squaring only part of the expression for $V_s$

tmjc-2023-other-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Requires applying the r.m.s. definition to a non-sinusoidal pulse waveform read from a graph.

tmjc-2023-other-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Standard interpretation of the photoelectric $E_{max}$–$f$ graph's gradient and intercept.
tmjc-2023-other-p1-q27.misconception: thinking the gradient depends on the metal

tmjc-2023-other-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Two-step substitution into $\Delta p = m\Delta v$ and the uncertainty principle.
tmjc-2023-other-p1-q28.misconception: using the full momentum instead of its uncertainty

tmjc-2023-other-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Requires identifying background count and correcting for it before and after halving.
tmjc-2023-other-p1-q30.misconception: applying half-life decay to the background count

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Simple everyday estimation of a cylinder volume.

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Straightforward area under an $a$–$t$ graph with a sign change.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q2.misconception: ignoring the sign of areas below the time axis

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires careful identification of which body each force acts on.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q3.misconception: thinking a Newton's 3rd-law pair can act on the same body

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Needs careful reading of the lines of action of eight forces on the diagram.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q4.misconception: assuming every force contributes a torque

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Direct application of upthrust equals weight for a floating body.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q5.misconception: confusing weight in N with mass in kg

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Students must realise the useful force is the tension difference (friction) and apply efficiency correctly.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q6.misconception: using the sum of tensions rather than their difference

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Direct use of $v = r\omega$ and a quarter-turn angle.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q7.misconception: confusing arc length with angular displacement

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Common trap of measuring distance from the surface instead of the centre.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q8.misconception: measuring $r$ from the Earth's surface instead of its centre

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Recognising that satellite mass cancels is a standard idea.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q9.misconception: thinking orbit radius depends on satellite mass

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Requires extracting $x_0$ and $v_0$ from a $v$–$x$ graph and knowing max-to-zero speed is a quarter cycle.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q10.misconception: taking the full period instead of a quarter period

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Requires converting a displacement–distance graph of a longitudinal wave into compressions and rarefactions, which many students find unintuitive.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q11.misconception: Thinking pressure is extreme where displacement is maximum

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Needs the intensity–amplitude relation and the realisation that amplitudes, not intensities, subtract at a minimum.

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Direct application of the rule for phase in a standing wave, read from the diagram.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q13.misconception: Using distance along the string to work out phase as for a progressive wave

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Straightforward kinetic-theory reasoning about a constant-volume heating.

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Tests standard definitions of internal energy and the first law.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q15.misconception: Internal energy depends only on temperature / heating is the only way to raise internal energy

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Requires the insight that the rate of heat loss is the same during cooling and freezing.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q16.misconception: Not equating the rates of heat loss before and during solidification

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Vector addition of two symmetric fields from a clear diagram.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q17.misconception: Assuming fields from equal and opposite charges cancel at an equidistant point

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q18.difficultyReason: A standard balanced-bridge network; spotting the redundant resistor is the only step.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q18.misconception: Assuming every resistor in a network carries current

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires redrawing the circuit to see the parallel combination before applying the potential divider.

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Qualitative reasoning about how removing a parallel branch redistributes p.d. in a series circuit.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q20.misconception: Thinking removing a bulb makes every remaining bulb brighter

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Needs $F = BIL\sin	heta$ for each segment plus Fleming's left-hand rule to get opposing directions.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q21.misconception: Adding force magnitudes without considering direction

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires applying the right-hand grip rule to three wires and adding the field vectors.

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Recognising that the field is uniform along the direction of motion gives the answer quickly.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q23.misconception: Thinking any motion of a coil in a magnetic field induces a current

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Requires reasoning about potential distribution in a rotating disc, an unfamiliar context.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming equal lengths of the disc give equal induced e.m.f.s

tmjc-2024-other-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Combines r.m.s.–peak conversion with $\omega = 2\pi f$ in a real-label context.
tmjc-2024-other-p1-q25.misconception: Using the r.m.s. value as the amplitude of the sinusoid

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Requires converting frequency to period and comparing with the screen width, with some prefix handling.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q11.misconception: Choosing a time-base without checking how many cycles fit on the screen

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Standard harmonic reasoning for a string fixed at both ends, read off a simple diagram.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q12.misconception: Thinking only odd harmonics are allowed on a string fixed at both ends

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q13.difficultyReason: One-line ratio from the grating equation; main risk is inverting the ratio.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q13.misconception: Inverting the ratio (higher order means shorter wavelength)

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Direct application of the first law with the sign convention for work on the gas.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming an insulated gas keeps a constant temperature

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Simple specific heat capacity calculation once the 50 °C equilibrium temperature is seen.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q15.misconception: Using the initial temperature difference instead of each block's temperature change

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Single proportionality step; the common trap is forgetting to square.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q16.misconception: Assuming temperature is proportional to r.m.s. speed rather than its square

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Requires separating force (same) from deflection and energy change (smaller for the heavier proton) and spotting the 'incorrect' wording.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q17.misconception: Thinking a heavier particle feels a smaller electric force

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The unusual circular layout disguises a simple parallel connection, which must be recognised before calculating.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q18.misconception: Assuming resistors drawn one after another are in series

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires reading several curves and using $R = V/I$ rather than the gradient.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q19.misconception: Taking resistance as the gradient of the I–V graph

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Combines LDR and NTC thermistor behaviour with a potential divider in which the voltmeter is across the fixed resistor.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q20.misconception: Thinking the voltmeter reading rises when the sensor resistances rise, regardless of where it is connected

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Two direction rules in sequence plus reversing for the negative charge.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q21.misconception: Forgetting to reverse the current direction for a negative charge

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Needs to realise the horizontal field gives a vertical force and use the 30° angle between wire and field.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q22.misconception: Ignoring the angle between the wire and the field

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Combines kinematics on an incline with the perpendicular velocity component in the e.m.f., then compares a non-obvious trade-off.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q23.misconception: Using the full speed rather than the component perpendicular to the field

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Requires keeping frequency fixed while increasing induced e.m.f., ruling out the tempting frequency change.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q24.misconception: Forgetting that changing supply frequency also changes the trace's frequency

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires finding r.m.s. values for sinusoidal, rectified and square waveforms.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q25.misconception: Treating every waveform's peak as if it were its r.m.s. value

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Students must trace current paths through a diode bridge for both half-cycles, which is less familiar than single-diode rectification.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q26.misconception: Thinking a diode circuit always gives half-wave output

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Standard two-step calculation from kinetic energy to momentum to de Broglie wavelength.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q27.misconception: Using the photon relation $\lambda = hc/E$ for an electron

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The calculation is one line, but students must recognise that the momentum uncertainty is along the slit width, perpendicular to the beam.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q28.misconception: Momentum uncertainty is along the direction of travel

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Direct recall of the conclusion of Rutherford's scattering experiment.

tmjc-2025-other-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Requires interpreting count-rate data against known penetrating powers, a standard exercise.
tmjc-2025-other-p1-q30.misconception: Thinking a few mm of aluminium does not stop β

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Students only need to recall and compare the prefix powers of ten.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Micro and milli represent the same factor.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Students must locate the rod’s centre of gravity and calculate both lever arms about the shifted pivot.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: The rod’s own centre of gravity shifts when the suspended mass is added.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: It requires finding the acceleration relative to the elevator before applying a standard motion equation.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must resolve the velocity perpendicular to the wall and account for its reversal.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Omitting the reversal of the normal velocity

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The ramp length must be calculated before frictional work can be included in the energy balance.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Using horizontal distance for frictional work

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The final speed must be resolved into components before using the vertical motion equation.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Treating gravity as an acceleration along the velocity

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: It requires distinguishing conservation of momentum from loss of kinetic energy.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Assuming momentum is lost in an inelastic collision

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student can identify the correct diagram by comparing the signed velocities.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The tension and orbital radius both change and must be included in the speed ratio.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must apply inverse-distance scaling and identify the sign of gravitational work.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Confusing the distance dependence of potential and field strength

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: It requires evaluating the kinetic-energy fraction at half amplitude and finding the remaining fraction.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Assuming energy varies linearly with displacement

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: It requires translating the spatial profile to infer the instantaneous direction and magnitude of particle velocity.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Reading particle velocity directly from the spatial slope

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: It requires finding the greatest allowed integer order and counting maxima on both sides of the centre.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The end conditions and node count determine how many quarter wavelengths fit in the pipe.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Miscounting quarter wavelengths between the end conditions

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must interpret the compression path, the cycle direction and the return to the original state.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Confusing work done by the gas with work done on it

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student applies the first law twice and takes the ratio of the resulting internal energy changes.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Assigning positive work on the gas during expansion

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: It requires identifying the fixed pressure and volume and forming a ratio using absolute temperatures.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Using Celsius temperatures in the ideal-gas equation

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student applies two familiar distance laws to the same change in separation.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must infer both the field direction and its changing strength from graph gradients.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Equating zero potential with zero electric field

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must combine the two charge flows and convert a per-minute count into current.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Subtracting currents for opposite charge motions

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student finds two equivalent capacitances and uses the same cell voltage for both.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Applying a factor of three to only one arrangement

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must infer the voltage division and square the voltage ratio to obtain the power split.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Assuming identical resistors always dissipate equal power

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The two voltmeters measure different parts of their potential dividers.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Assuming both voltmeters measure the variable resistor.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must reverse the electron’s direction to apply Fleming’s left-hand rule.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Treating electron motion as conventional current.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The calculation combines magnetic force on a wire with the principle of moments.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Using the full side length as the length in the field.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The rotating disc requires tracking the radial dependence and sign of the induced e.m.f.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Adding the two centre-to-point e.m.f. magnitudes along QOS.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: One transformer ratio gives both requested values with straightforward arithmetic.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The comparison links energy gained through a potential difference to momentum and wavelength.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Assuming equal kinetic energies imply equal momenta.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must halve successive drops because the measured rate includes a constant background.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Applying the half-life to the measured total.

tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must track both nucleon and proton numbers through several decays.
tmjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Reading mass number as neutron number.

vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Simple order-of-magnitude estimates; converting 300 K to 27 °C makes D obvious.

vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Requires area under a v–t graph with a negative region and distinguishing distance from displacement.
vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Treating area below the time axis as positive displacement

vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires realising the force fixes the acceleration direction but not the direction of motion.
vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: The direction of motion must be the direction of the resultant force

vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Needs the idea that upthrust depends only on the displaced volume, not on what is inside the cube.
vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Water entering the cube increases the upthrust

vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Requires checking conservation of total energy and the zero-KE condition at the lowest point.
vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Maximum speed occurs at the lowest point

vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Requires resolving weight along the incline, using $P = Fv$, and adding the constant friction power.
vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Using the full weight rather than its component along the slope

vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Direct application of $\omega = 2\pi f$ for a rigid rotating body.
vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Confusing angular velocity with linear speed

vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Standard Kepler's third law ratio with an irrelevant change in satellite mass as a distractor.
vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Orbital period depends on the satellite's mass

vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Single substitution into $pV = NkT$ with a temperature conversion.
vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Using temperature in °C in the ideal gas equation

vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Combines $pV = NkT$ with $\frac{1}{2}m\langle c^2 \rangle = \frac{3}{2}kT$ and a square-root scaling.
vjc-2024-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: The r.m.s. speed is proportional to temperature

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Requires combining P = Fv with drag ∝ v² to get P ∝ v³, then a cube-root ratio.
vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Assuming maximum speed is proportional to power

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Straightforward energy conservation, but students often forget the extra compression distance in the GPE term.
vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Forgetting the extra drop during compression

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Single application of Newton's second law in a vertical circle.
vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Ignoring or subtracting weight at the top of a vertical circle

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Recognising that orbital radius is mass-independent while forces and energies scale with mass.
vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Thinking orbit radius depends on satellite mass

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Measuring distance from the surface instead of the centre

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Requires realising PE has twice the frequency of the motion, so the 2 s window is only half a period.
vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Assuming the energy graph has the same period as the oscillation

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Applying ⟨KE⟩ = 3/2 kT and v_rms ∝ 1/√m to two gases.
vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Thinking heavier gas atoms have more kinetic energy at the same temperature

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Conceptual: phase difference between fixed points on a progressive wave is constant.
vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Confusing phase difference with displacement varying in time

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires measuring the total angle from the original polarisation and expressing the answer relative to I30.
vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Applying Malus' law to the incremental 30° rotation instead of the total angle

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Simple reasoning about loops per wavelength when frequency doubles.

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Chains volume, mass, force balance and charge quantisation with powers of ten.

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Standard recall of the filament lamp I–V characteristic.
vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Thinking a lamp has zero resistance when cold

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Requires spotting that P is short-circuited and Q, R are in parallel before applying power and potential-divider ideas.

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Combines Fleming's left-hand rule on a 3D diagram with F = BIL and I = Ne/t.
vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Treating electron flow as the same direction as conventional current

vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires knowing the disc e.m.f. scales with r² and taking a difference between two radii.
vjc-2025-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Assuming the disc e.m.f. is proportional to radius

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The student must express energy and charge in base units and match exponents.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Inverting the units of charge rather than cancelling the current units.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Identifying the curves requires relating speed to the height gradient and drag to resultant force.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Treating a falling height curve as a falling speed curve.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student distinguishes free fall from situations where a contact force supports the person.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: A stationary object under static friction supplies a counterexample to the claim that friction always dissipates energy.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The calculation uses the component of a given force along a given displacement.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Using the full pulling force for horizontal work.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish extension from total length and find the area against the correct axis.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Treating length as extension or using the area against the force axis.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must recognise zero tension and resolve weight along the inward radius.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Using the component of weight perpendicular to the radius.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must derive the orbital speed dependence before comparing kinetic energies.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Comparing kinetic energies using mass alone.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must compare the slope of the displacement graph with the direction of the restoring acceleration.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Reading the sign of displacement as the sign of acceleration.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must read an energy–position pair and connect it to angular frequency and period.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using the full horizontal span as the displacement.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must use the direction of travel to identify which zero crossing will reach Q first.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using the nearest crossing on the wrong side of Q.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The calculation requires converting the percentage reduction to a transmitted fraction before applying Malus’ law.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Using the percentage lost as the percentage transmitted.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Find the grating spacing, then calculate and subtract two diffraction angles.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Confusing an angle from the grating normal with the angular separation.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Relate the angular position of the first minimum to the width measured on the screen.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Confusing angular width with width on the screen.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Identify the two phase-change plateaus and compare their durations at constant heating power.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Comparing plateau temperatures instead of durations.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Combine the ideal-gas law with the kinetic-energy relation before taking the speed ratio.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Treating r.m.s. speed as proportional to the pressure–volume product.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Use the isothermal condition and the work sign convention to infer the heat-transfer sign.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Reversing the signs of work done on and by a gas.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Calculate the trapezium area and apply the negative sign in the potential gradient.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Using the slope of the field graph or reversing the sign for an electron.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Add the signed potentials from two charges at different distances, then multiply by the test charge.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Using the inverse-square field law for potential.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Connect number density to total electron count and recognize that the cross-sectional area cancels.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Confusing number density with the total number of electrons.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Track how the voltmeter reading, series current, internal voltage drop and LDR resistance change together.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Equating the fixed-resistor voltage with the cell terminal voltage.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Combine the magnetic-force equation with torque balance using the correct moment arms.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Confusing the length of wire in the field with a moment arm.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Identify the current–field angle for each side and use the opposite current directions on the vertical sides.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Assuming every segment of a current loop experiences a magnetic force.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Read the time spent at each voltage and weight the squared levels over one period.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Find the motional emf and determine its polarity relative to the direction of flight.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Reversing the direction of magnetic force on positive charge.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Differentiate the flux linkage and use the coil area and angular frequency in SI units.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Confusing frequency in hertz with angular frequency.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Recognize that the maximum and minimum of the wavefunction have the same squared magnitude.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Treating the signed wavefunction as probability density.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Convert the proton energy to joules, calculate its momentum uncertainty, and apply the syllabus uncertainty relation.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Using the full momentum or the percentage alone for momentum uncertainty.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Translate the two decay types into grid displacements and identify the parent two steps from Y.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Changing mass number in beta-minus decay.

vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Subtract the background before applying two half-lives and restore it to obtain the detector reading.
vjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Applying radioactive decay to the background count.

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Two short steps: scale the force with v² and apply P = Fv.
yijc-2022-promo-p1-q11.misconception: Using the force at the original speed when computing power at the new speed

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Direct use of power = work/time and the efficiency ratio.
yijc-2022-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Multiplying by efficiency instead of dividing to find input power

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Single-step ω = 2π/T once the 12-hour period is recognised.
