yijc-2022-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Confusing the hour hand's period with 24 h or 1 h

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Needs the radius to include the 3.0 m arm, then resolving tension to find ω and the period.
yijc-2022-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Taking the radius as only the string's horizontal extent, ignoring the arm

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Combines apparent weight on a rotating planet with the constant-density result g ∝ R, which students often miss.
yijc-2022-promo-p1-q16.misconception: Assuming g ∝ 1/R² when the radius changes at constant density

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Standard substitution into U = −GMm/r at two radii.
yijc-2022-promo-p1-q17.misconception: Using mgh for large height changes where g is not constant

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q18.misconception: Confusing period, frequency and angular frequency

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Needs the qualitative link between reduced damping and a taller, sharper resonance curve.
yijc-2022-promo-p1-q20.misconception: Thinking damping changes only the width, not the peak height

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Straightforward v = fλ then phase difference = 2πx/λ.

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Needs careful reasoning about phase lag and direction of travel without a diagram.
yijc-2022-promo-p1-q22.misconception: Getting the direction of phase lag wrong for a progressive wave

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Standard Malus' law with the halving at the first polariser.
yijc-2022-promo-p1-q23.misconception: Applying Malus' law directly to unpolarised light

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Standard properties of stationary waves (phase across nodes, amplitude variation).
yijc-2022-promo-p1-q24.misconception: Thinking all points of a standing wave vibrate in phase

yijc-2022-promo-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires knowing that displacement nodes are pressure antinodes for sound.
yijc-2022-promo-p1-q25.misconception: Assuming displacement and pressure nodes coincide

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Standard fractional uncertainty for a cubic dependence.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Forgetting to multiply the fractional uncertainty by the power

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: A standard equal-displacement kinematics problem with one quadratic.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Taking the overtaking moment as when the speeds are equal

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the two bodies in a third-law pair, a common but well-drilled idea.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Confusing balanced forces on one body with a Newton's third law pair

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Needs a connected-body analysis with an incline component and friction in two steps.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Taking tension equal to the hanging weight even when the system accelerates

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: A direct application of the principle of moments followed by recognising an inverse-proportion graph.

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Requires knowing the concurrency condition for three forces and checking it carefully on diagrams.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Thinking that balanced force magnitudes alone guarantee equilibrium, ignoring torque

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Each statement tests a basic energy or momentum fact.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Believing no device can ever be 100% efficient

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Recall of centripetal force direction and that a perpendicular force does no work.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Believing there is an outward (centrifugal) net force, or that a force always does work over a distance

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the lowest point as the critical position and converting weight to mass.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming the critical position in a vertical circle is always the top

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Simple recognition that horizontal motion does no work against a vertical field.

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Requires linking plateau length to energy supplied at constant power.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Thinking a higher phase-change temperature implies a larger latent heat

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Single application of the ideal gas equation to the combined gas, with unit conversion.

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Requires deducing amplitude from distance per cycle and chaining frequency, angular frequency and KE.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Taking the distance per oscillation as two amplitudes rather than four

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Computing wavelength then reducing a phase difference above one cycle.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Inverting the ratio of separation to wavelength

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Thinking the source-to-slit distance affects fringe spacing

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Needs the first-minimum condition plus the doubling for the full central width.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Taking the half-width as the full width of the central maximum

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: A standard null-point problem with Coulomb's law. It only needs a square root of the charge ratio.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Forgetting the inverse-square dependence on distance

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: A direct force balance using $E = V/d$.

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Needs the constant-volume link between length and area as well as $R = \rho L/A$.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Forgetting that the cross-sectional area changes when the length changes at constant volume

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: A routine internal-resistance argument, but students may confuse the terminal p.d. with the p.d. across $r$.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Confusing the terminal p.d. with the p.d. across the internal resistance

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Seeing that the 70 Ω resistor is in parallel with the other three in series is the only real step.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Misidentifying series and parallel combinations in a diamond network

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The right-hand grip rule applied in a plan view.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Thinking the field points towards or away from the wire instead of tangentially

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Students must separate each wire's own field from the field acting on it, and apply Newton's third law to the forces.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Thinking the wire with the larger current experiences the larger force

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Needs Lenz's law applied to both the pole and the end being changed, plus Faraday's law for the size.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Thinking that changing the pole always reverses the current, regardless of which end it enters

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Equates two power expressions, one of which uses the r.m.s. current.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Treating r.m.s. current as needing a further $\sqrt{2}$ conversion

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: A standard recall of wave versus particle evidence.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Confusing evidence for the wave nature of particles with evidence for the particle nature of light

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: A direct use of the photoelectric equation, with the work function given as a threshold frequency.

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: A direct recall of the conclusion of the Rutherford scattering experiment.

yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The trap is normalising the count rate per unit mass before counting half-lives.
yijc-2023-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Comparing count rates of samples with different masses without normalising

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Standard propagation of fractional uncertainty with correct rounding.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Adding absolute uncertainties for a product

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Two chained kinematics equations with a unit conversion.

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Standard two-body connected system: find common acceleration, then isolate the trailer.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Forgetting to include resistive forces when isolating one body

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Requires choosing pivots and comparing moment arms rather than just balancing vertical forces.

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Read the limit of proportionality off the graph and find a triangle's area, remembering the natural length offset.

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Single resolution of weight along an incline followed by $W = Fs$.

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Direct efficiency calculation from two work-done products.

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Novel context: must realise one sound period corresponds to 1/16 of a revolution.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Treating the sound frequency as the rotation frequency

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Needs the relation $TE = -KE$ for circular orbits and reasoning with mass as a variable.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Thinking a more massive satellite has more negative total energy

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Requires careful sign handling across three work steps and the definition of potential.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Sign confusion between work done to infinity and work done from infinity

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Energy balance with specific heat and latent heat; arithmetic is routine.

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Single proportionality, but the square is a common trap.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Taking temperature proportional to r.m.s. speed

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Direct recall of the effect of damping on a resonance curve.

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Must identify the full repeating unit in a complex waveform before using the time-base.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Taking the time between any two pulses as the period

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Unusual combination of Malus' law with coherent superposition of amplitudes.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Adding intensities instead of amplitudes for coherent waves

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Must identify the current mode from the diagram and know only odd harmonics exist in a closed tube.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Thinking the next resonance adds a half wavelength rather than stepping to the next odd quarter

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: One-line ratio from the grating equation.

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Requires resolving Coulomb forces in two dimensions and deducing the sign of Q from the direction of the net force.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Ignoring that only a component of the diagonal force cancels the perpendicular force

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: A one-line relation, but the negative charge makes sign errors likely.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Forgetting the negative sign of the charge when computing potential energy

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Straightforward ratio with $R = \rho l/A$, but three quantities change at once and area depends on diameter squared.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Treating cross-sectional area as proportional to diameter

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Standard pair of simultaneous equations from $E = I(R + r)$.

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Needs the balance condition plus a potential divider over the whole driver circuit including the series resistor.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Applying the potential divider to the wire alone, forgetting the series resistor carries the same current

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Two field formulas plus reading current directions from the diagram to decide whether the fields add or subtract.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Adding magnetic fields without considering their directions

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Standard application of forces between parallel currents with an inverse-distance comparison.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming equal and opposite forces on the two sides of the loop cancel

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Combines the direction of force on moving charges with resolving the rod length perpendicular to the velocity.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Using the full rod length instead of its component perpendicular to the velocity

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Direct use of $I_0/\sqrt{2}$ and mean power = half peak power once the student sees rectification does not change the r.m.s. value.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Thinking rectification changes the r.m.s. value, or using peak power as average power

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Standard photoelectric facts that are drilled heavily.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Threshold condition stated as a minimum wavelength instead of a maximum

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Needs knowledge of continuous vs characteristic X-ray features and the cut-off wavelength.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Confusing the cut-off (minimum) wavelength with a maximum wavelength

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Thinking alpha particles miss whole atoms or bounce off a surface

yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Simple bookkeeping of nucleon and proton numbers through two decays.
yijc-2024-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Confusing neutron number with nucleon number

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Use typical everyday and atomic scales to evaluate four different estimates.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Confusing everyday or atomic orders of magnitude.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Rearrange the vectors tip to tail while preserving their directions to check for zero resultant.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Taking any triangular arrangement to mean zero vector sum.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires balancing both moments and vertical forces.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Treating both rod forces as upward.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the two bodies in one gravitational interaction.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Confusing balanced forces with a third-law pair.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Requires finding and adding the times for two successive stages.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Requires converting minutes to seconds and applying efficiency to the power balance.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Requires relating impact speed to energy while distinguishing vertical distance from displacement.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Assuming launch direction changes impact speed.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Requires matching momentum-change magnitudes and solving for the speed-change ratio.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Confusing equal impulses with equal velocity changes.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Both quantities follow directly from their radius dependence at fixed angular velocity.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Equating constant angular velocity with constant linear speed.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing mass-dependent quantities from quantities fixed by the common orbit.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Confusing gravitational force with gravitational acceleration.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Requires inferring relative damping from free oscillations and applying it to forced response curves.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Expecting stronger damping to raise the resonance peak.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Requires finding the incident angle at the inserted filter and applying Malus’ law twice.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Using the angle between filters for both transmissions.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Requires converting intensities to amplitudes before combining and squaring them.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires converting line density to spacing, finding the highest integer order and counting both sides.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Requires equating mean kinetic energies and taking a square root.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Assuming equal temperatures imply equal r.m.s. speeds.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Requires recognising the common pressure and relating gas mass to volume and temperature.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Assuming the volumes alone determine the mass ratio.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Requires tracking the signs of heat, work and internal energy during isobaric expansion.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Using the sign of work done by the gas for work done on it.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing thermal equilibrium from equality of total energy and radiation rates.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Equating temperature with total internal energy.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Requires chaining charge transfer, capacitance and uniform-field relations.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Multiplying by capacitance to find the voltage change.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Requires equating heating powers and taking the square root of the resistance ratio.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Treating the steady current as the AC peak current.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires relating local wire thickness to the gradient of cumulative resistance.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Confusing local resistance per unit length with total resistance.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Requires tracking total current, lost volts and redistribution between the parallel branches.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Assuming both branch currents fall when the terminal voltage falls.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The diagram requires several series and parallel reductions.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Grouping resistors by appearance instead of shared nodes.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must resolve the magnetic force relative to the vertical wire.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Assuming the magnetic force acts along the line separating the wires.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The expression follows once the normal component of the field is identified.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Using the angle to the plane as the angle to the normal.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The calculation combines photon energy from wavelength with a milliwatt-to-watt conversion.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Treating power as the energy of a single photon.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must identify which coordinate the slit confines before applying the uncertainty relation.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Assigning the uncertainty to the direction of travel.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The daughter-to-parent ratio must be converted to a surviving fraction before using the decay law.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Confusing the daughter-to-parent ratio with the initial-to-remaining ratio.

yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must convert per-nucleon binding energies into totals and account for energy released.
yijc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Counting free neutrons as bound nucleons.
